about: Plain-English guides to the systems behind Magic interactions, and verified rulings for common and tricky interactions. Every rule number refers to the Comprehensive Rules. Shared by the desktop app, and later the website and mobile app.

concepts.title: Priority and the stack
summary: Spells and most abilities don't happen right away: they go on the stack and wait. The stack resolves one object at a time, last in, first out, so the most recent spell or ability resolves first.

After anything is put on the stack, the active player gets priority first. Players pass priority in turn order. When every player passes in a row, the top object resolves, and the active player gets priority again. If everyone passes with the stack empty, the step or phase ends.

You can respond to anything on the stack. You can't respond to things that don't use the stack: playing a land, mana abilities, special actions like turning a face-down creature face up, or state-based actions. You can respond to abilities those trigger, though.
When a spell or ability tries to resolve, it checks its targets. If every target is now illegal, it doesn't resolve at all. If only some are illegal, it resolves and simply doesn't affect those.

concepts.title: APNAP order
summary: APNAP stands for Active Player, NonActive Player. Whenever players would make choices or take actions at the same time, the active player (whose turn it is) goes first, then the other players in turn order.

Triggered abilities: when several trigger at once, the active player puts all of theirs on the stack first, in any order they like, then each other player does the same in turn order. Because the stack is last in, first out, the last player's triggers resolve first and the active player's resolve last.
Example: during your upkeep, your trigger and your opponent's trigger both happen. You put yours on the stack first, your opponent puts theirs on top, so your opponent's resolves first.
Simultaneous choices work the same way: for "each player sacrifices a creature", the active player chooses first, then each other player in turn order, and then all of them are sacrificed at once.

concepts.title: Combat
summary: Combat has five steps: beginning of combat, declare attackers, declare blockers, combat damage, end of combat.
A creature only becomes "blocked" or "unblocked" in the declare blockers step. Abilities that need an unblocked attacker, like ninjutsu, can only be used from that point on.

First strike and double strike: if any attacking or blocking creature has either at the start of the combat damage step, there are two damage steps. In the first, only creatures with first strike or double strike deal damage. In the second, creatures with double strike deal damage again, along with every creature that didn't deal first-strike damage, including creatures that joined the combat after the first step (such as a Ninja put in with ninjutsu).
All combat damage in a step is dealt at the same time, and lifelink's life gain happens at that same moment.

Trample: the attacker must assign lethal damage to its blockers before assigning the rest to the player. With deathtouch, 1 damage counts as lethal. Protection doesn't lower that lethal amount, even though the damage to the protected blocker will be prevented.

concepts.title: State-based actions
summary: State-based actions are game checks that happen automatically whenever a player would receive priority. They don't use the stack, and nobody can respond to them.

Among them: a player with 0 or less life loses; a player with ten or more poison counters loses; a creature with 0 or less toughness is put into its owner's graveyard (this isn't destruction, so indestructible doesn't save it); a creature with lethal damage marked on it, or any damage from a deathtouch source, is destroyed (indestructible does save it); a planeswalker with 0 loyalty goes to the graveyard; an Aura attached to nothing goes to the graveyard; +1/+1 and -1/-1 counters on the same permanent cancel out in pairs.

Legend rule: if you control two or more legendary permanents with the same name, you choose one and the rest go to the graveyard. That's not sacrificing or destroying, so abilities that care about those don't trigger.
All the state-based actions that apply happen at the same time, then the game checks again, until none apply.

concepts.title: Layers and continuous effects
summary: When several continuous effects change a permanent, they're applied in a fixed order of layers, no matter when each effect started: 1 copy effects (and face-down status), 2 control, 3 text, 4 types, 5 color, 6 abilities being added or removed, 7 power and toughness.

Power and toughness (layer 7) has its own order: 7a characteristic-defining abilities ("its power is equal to…"), 7b effects that set power and toughness ("becomes a 1/1"), 7c effects and counters that modify them (+3/+3, anthems, +1/+1 counters), 7d effects that switch power and toughness.

Examples: a 2/2 under Glorious Anthem hit by Turn to Frog becomes a 1/1 (7b) and then gets +1/+1 (7c): a 2/2. A creature with Giant Growth that later becomes 1/1 is still 4/4, because the +3/+3 applies after the set. Under Humility, a creature with three +1/+1 counters is 4/4.

Within a layer, effects apply in timestamp order (oldest first), unless one depends on another. An effect depends on another if applying the other would change whether it exists, what it applies to, or what it does. Then the other one applies first. Example: Blood Moon removes Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth's ability, so Urborg's effect depends on Blood Moon's. Blood Moon applies first, Urborg loses its ability, and no lands become Swamps.

concepts.title: Replacement and prevention effects
summary: Replacement effects change an event as it happens, rather than responding to it. You can spot them by words like "instead", "skip", "enters with" or "as this enters". They don't use the stack, and nobody can respond to them.
Prevention effects ("prevent the next 3 damage") are a kind of replacement effect for damage.

When several replacement or prevention effects would apply to the same event, the affected player, or the controller of the affected object, chooses one to apply, then checks whether the others still apply, and so on. Each effect can apply to a given event only once.

concepts.title: Triggered abilities
summary: Triggered abilities start with "When", "Whenever" or "At". When their event happens they trigger, and they're put on the stack the next time a player would receive priority, after state-based actions are checked. Their controller chooses targets then.
Once on the stack, a triggered ability is independent of its source. Destroying the source doesn't stop it.
Leaves-the-battlefield triggers "look back in time": they see the game as it was just before the event. That's why Blood Artist triggers for every creature that dies at the same time it does.
"When/Whenever X, if Y, …" (an intervening "if" clause) checks Y both when it would trigger and again when it resolves.

concepts.title: Zone changes and new objects
summary: When a card moves from one zone to another, it becomes a brand-new object with no memory of where it was. That's why a flickered (exiled and returned) creature loses "until end of turn" effects, counters, damage and Auras, and why it has summoning sickness again.
A commander that dies goes to the graveyard first, so "when a creature dies" abilities trigger. Its owner may then move it to the command zone.

concepts.title: Copies
summary: A copy only gets the original's copiable values: its printed characteristics, as changed by other copy effects and a few "as this enters" choices. It doesn't copy counters, Auras or Equipment, stat boosts, other effects, or whether it's tapped.
A copy of a spell keeps the original's choices, like modes, targets (unless the effect lets you change them) and the value of X.
A copy of a permanent spell becomes a token as it resolves.

concepts.title: Casting spells and costs
summary: Casting a spell follows a fixed order: announce it, choose modes, choose X and other values, choose targets, work out the total cost, activate mana abilities, then pay.

Total cost is the mana cost (or an alternative cost) plus additional costs and cost increases, minus reductions. Commander tax is an additional {2} for each time that commander was previously cast from the command zone.

Timing: sorceries, creatures, artifacts, enchantments, planeswalkers and battles can only be cast in your main phase, while the stack is empty. Instants, and anything with flash, can be cast any time you have priority.

concepts.title: Special actions and mana
summary: Special actions don't use the stack and can't be responded to. They include playing a land, turning a face-down creature face up, and a few others. Abilities they trigger can be responded to.
Mana abilities resolve immediately and can't be responded to. You can activate them whenever you have priority, or while you're paying a cost.
Split second stops players from casting spells and activating abilities other than mana abilities while it's on the stack. Mana abilities and special actions are still allowed.
Unspent mana empties from your mana pool at the end of each step and phase. There's no mana burn: you don't lose life for it.

concepts.title: Summoning sickness
summary: A creature can't attack, and can't use abilities with {T} or {Q} in their cost, unless you've controlled it continuously since your most recent turn began. This applies to creatures you just cast, gained control of, or flickered.
Haste removes this restriction. Abilities without {T} or {Q} in their cost can be used right away.

concepts.title: Commander
summary: Decks have exactly 100 cards including the commander, with no duplicates except basic lands. Every card must fit the commander's color identity: the colors of all mana symbols in its mana cost and rules text (hybrid symbols count as both colors; reminder text doesn't count). Players start at 40 life.
Your commander starts in the command zone. Each time you cast it from there, it costs {2} more for each previous time.

If your commander goes to the graveyard or exile, you may move it to the command zone (it goes there first, so "dies" triggers happen). If it would go to your hand or library, you may put it in the command zone instead.
A player dealt 21 or more combat damage by the same commander over the game loses, no matter who controlled that commander. In multiplayer, your first mulligan is free.

concepts.title: Targets, hexproof and protection
summary: Targets are chosen when a spell is cast or an ability is put on the stack, and checked again when it resolves.

Hexproof: can't be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control. Shroud: can't be the target of any spells or abilities. Neither stops effects that don't target, like "destroy all creatures".

Protection from a quality means (DEBT): Damage from sources with that quality is prevented, it can't be Enchanted or Equipped by such things, it can't be Blocked by creatures with that quality, and it can't be Targeted by such spells or abilities.

concepts.title: Commander Brackets
summary: Commander Brackets are Wizards' optional 1 to 5 scale for finding Commander games with people who want the same kind of game: 1 Exhibition, 2 Core, 3 Upgraded, 4 Optimized, 5 cEDH. They aren't part of the Comprehensive Rules and aren't enforced by judges; you agree on them with your pod before the game (rule zero).

Each bracket has an intent and a rough game length: Exhibition decks put a theme over power and expect at least nine turns, Core decks are straightforward and expect at least eight, Upgraded decks have strong synergy and expect at least six, Optimized decks are built to win fast and expect at least four, and cEDH games can end on any turn.

Game Changers are a list of cards that warp Commander games. Brackets 1 and 2 have none, Bracket 3 allows up to three, and Brackets 4 and 5 allow any number. A commander on the list counts toward the limit.

The other limits: no two-card infinite combos in Brackets 1 and 2 and no early-game ones in Bracket 3; no mass land denial below Bracket 4; no extra-turn cards in Bracket 1, and only a few, never chained or looped, in Brackets 2 and 3. Tutors have no limit of their own since October 2025: the best ones are Game Changers.

The deck builder shows which bracket a Commander deck's cards fit, lets you pick the bracket you're aiming for, and marks the cards that break it. The Formats section has the full bracket descriptions and the current Game Changers list.

interactions.question: I attack with a creature that has first strike and it isn't blocked. After first-strike combat damage is dealt, I activate ninjutsu to return it to my hand and put a Ninja onto the battlefield tapped and attacking. Will the Ninja deal combat damage this turn?
interactions.explanation: There are two combat damage steps because a creature had first strike. The Ninja didn't deal first-strike damage, so it deals damage in the second (regular) combat damage step. Your first striker deals its damage and then gets picked back up.

interactions.question: Can I activate ninjutsu during the declare attackers step, before blockers are declared?
interactions.explanation: Ninjutsu needs an unblocked attacking creature, and a creature only becomes blocked or unblocked in the declare blockers step.

interactions.question: My 2/2 creature with double strike is blocked by a 3/3 creature with no abilities. Do both creatures die?
interactions.explanation: First-strike damage step: the 2/2 deals 2 to the 3/3, which survives. Regular damage step: the 2/2 deals 2 more (4 total, lethal) while the 3/3 deals 3 to it at the same time. Both die.

interactions.question: A 5/5 attacking creature with trample is blocked by a 2/2. What is the most combat damage it can assign to the defending player?
interactions.explanation: It has to assign lethal damage (2) to the blocker first; the other 3 can go to the player.

interactions.question: A 5/5 attacking creature with trample and deathtouch is blocked by a 4/4. What is the most combat damage it can assign to the defending player?
interactions.explanation: With deathtouch, 1 damage counts as lethal, so it assigns 1 to the blocker and 4 to the player.

interactions.question: A green 4/4 attacking creature with trample is blocked by a 2/2 with protection from green. What is the most combat damage it can assign to the defending player?
interactions.explanation: It still has to assign lethal damage (2) to the blocker, even though protection will prevent that damage. The remaining 2 can go to the player.

interactions.question: It's my upkeep. I control a permanent with "At the beginning of your upkeep" and my opponent controls one with "At the beginning of each upkeep". Both trigger. Whose trigger resolves first?
interactions.explanation: APNAP: as the active player you put your trigger on the stack first, then your opponent puts theirs on top. The stack resolves last in, first out, so your opponent's resolves first.

interactions.question: In a four-player game, it's player A's turn and turn order is A, B, C, D. Each player controls an ability that triggers at the same moment. Whose ability resolves first?
interactions.explanation: Triggers go on the stack in APNAP order: A, then B, C, D. D's ends up on top, so it resolves first and A's resolves last.

interactions.question: Can I cast an instant in response to my opponent playing a land, before the land enters the battlefield?
interactions.explanation: Playing a land is a special action: it doesn't use the stack, so there's nothing to respond to. You can respond to any abilities it triggers, like landfall.

interactions.question: A permanent's triggered ability is on the stack, and I destroy that permanent in response. Does the triggered ability still resolve?
interactions.explanation: Once on the stack, an ability is independent of its source. It resolves anyway, using the source's last known information if it needs any.

interactions.question: My opponent casts a spell with split second. Can I activate a mana ability while it's on the stack?
interactions.explanation: Split second stops spells and non-mana abilities, but mana abilities and special actions are still allowed.

interactions.question: My opponent casts a spell with split second. Can I cast an instant in response?
interactions.explanation: While a spell with split second is on the stack, no player can cast spells or activate abilities other than mana abilities.

interactions.question: While a spell with split second is on the stack, can I turn a face-down morph creature face up?
interactions.explanation: Turning a face-down creature face up is a special action, which split second doesn't stop.

interactions.question: I cast a spell that targets my opponent's creature. In response, that creature gains hexproof. Does my spell resolve and have any effect?
interactions.explanation: Hexproof makes it an illegal target for your spells. With its only target illegal, the spell doesn't resolve.

interactions.question: I cast a spell that targets two of my opponent's creatures. In response, one of them gains hexproof. Does my spell still affect the other creature?
interactions.explanation: A spell with at least one legal target still resolves; it just doesn't affect the illegal target.

interactions.question: My creature has indestructible and gets -3/-3 until end of turn, making its toughness 0. Does it go to the graveyard?
interactions.explanation: A creature with 0 toughness is put into its owner's graveyard as a state-based action. That isn't destruction, so indestructible doesn't help.

interactions.question: When the legend rule makes me put a legendary permanent into the graveyard, does that count as sacrificing it?
interactions.explanation: The legend rule puts the others into the graveyard as a state-based action. It isn't a sacrifice, so "whenever you sacrifice" abilities don't trigger ("dies" abilities do).

interactions.question: I'm at 2 life. In combat, my creature with lifelink deals 3 damage while I'm dealt 5 combat damage at the same time. Do I lose the game?
interactions.explanation: Combat damage is dealt all at once, and lifelink's gain happens at the same moment: 2 + 3 - 5 = 0. At 0 life you lose when state-based actions are checked.

interactions.question: A 2/2 creature gets +1/+1 from Glorious Anthem. Then Turn to Frog makes it lose all abilities and become a blue Frog with base power and toughness 1/1. What are its power and toughness now?
interactions.explanation: Setting power and toughness (layer 7b) applies before modifying them (7c), whatever the timestamps. It becomes 1/1, then gets +1/+1 from the Anthem.

interactions.question: A 2/2 creature gets +3/+3 from Giant Growth this turn. Afterwards, an effect sets its base power and toughness to 1/1. What are its power and toughness now?
interactions.explanation: The newer "becomes 1/1" effect applies in layer 7b, and Giant Growth's +3/+3 still applies after it in 7c.

interactions.question: Humility is on the battlefield (all creatures lose all abilities and have base power and toughness 1/1). A creature there has three +1/+1 counters on it. What are its power and toughness?
interactions.explanation: Humility sets it to 1/1 in layer 7b; the counters add +3/+3 in layer 7c.

interactions.question: Blood Moon and Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth are both on the battlefield. Are my other nonbasic lands Swamps?
interactions.explanation: Both are type-changing effects in layer 4, but Blood Moon removes Urborg's ability, so Urborg's effect depends on Blood Moon's. Blood Moon applies first, Urborg becomes a Mountain with no abilities, and nothing becomes a Swamp.

interactions.question: Clone enters as a copy of a creature that has two +1/+1 counters on it. Does Clone get those counters?
interactions.explanation: Counters aren't copiable values; Clone copies only the printed characteristics.

interactions.question: A spell with {X} in its mana cost is copied. Does the copy have the same value of X?
interactions.explanation: A copy of a spell copies the choices made when it was cast, including the value of X.

interactions.question: Blood Artist and three other creatures are destroyed at the same time by a board wipe. Does Blood Artist's ability trigger for the other three creatures?
interactions.explanation: "Dies" abilities are leaves-the-battlefield abilities that look back in time, so Blood Artist sees every creature that dies with it (and itself).

interactions.question: A creature got +2/+2 until end of turn, then was exiled and returned to the battlefield in the same turn. Does it still have +2/+2?
interactions.explanation: It came back as a new object with no memory of its previous existence, so earlier effects on it no longer apply.

interactions.question: Two replacement effects from different players' permanents would both apply to damage that's about to be dealt to me. Who chooses the order they apply in?
interactions.explanation: The affected player (or the controller of the affected object) chooses which replacement effect applies first.

interactions.question: A creature I control would die. One effect says to exile it instead; my opponent controls a different effect saying to shuffle it into its owner's library instead. Who chooses which applies?
interactions.explanation: As the controller of the affected creature, you choose which replacement effect to apply.

interactions.question: I gained control of my opponent's creature this turn. It doesn't have haste. Can I attack with it this turn?
interactions.explanation: You haven't controlled it continuously since your most recent turn began.

interactions.question: A creature without haste came under my control this turn. Can I activate one of its abilities that has {T} in the cost?
interactions.explanation: Summoning sickness stops {T} and {Q} abilities as well as attacking. Abilities without those symbols in the cost are fine.

interactions.question: At the end of a step, do I lose life for mana left unspent in my mana pool?
interactions.explanation: Unspent mana just empties from your pool at the end of each step and phase. Mana burn no longer exists.

interactions.question: My commander has been cast from the command zone twice this game. How much additional generic mana does it cost to cast it from the command zone a third time?
interactions.explanation: Commander tax is {2} more for each previous time it was cast from the command zone: 2 x 2 = {4}.

interactions.question: I gain control of my opponent's commander and deal combat damage with it to a third player. Does that damage count toward the 21 commander damage from that commander?
interactions.explanation: Commander damage counts damage from the same commander, whoever controls it.

interactions.question: My commander dies. Does it go to the graveyard first, so that abilities that trigger when a creature dies trigger?
interactions.explanation: A commander going to the graveyard or exile gets there first; its owner may then move it to the command zone as a state-based action.

interactions.question: My commander would be shuffled into my library. May I put it into the command zone instead?
interactions.explanation: For the hand or library it's a replacement effect: it can go straight to the command zone instead.

interactions.question: Does a hybrid mana symbol like {W/U} in a card's mana cost count as both white and blue for color identity?
interactions.explanation: Color identity includes every color of every mana symbol in the mana cost and rules text, so a hybrid symbol counts as both.

interactions.question: In a multiplayer Commander game, is my first mulligan free (I don't put any cards on the bottom)?
interactions.explanation: In multiplayer games (and Brawl), the first mulligan doesn't count toward the cards you put on the bottom.

interactions.question: A creature with undying that has a +1/+1 counter on it dies. Does undying return it to the battlefield?
interactions.explanation: Undying only returns it if it had no +1/+1 counters on it when it died.

interactions.question: A creature with persist that has a +1/+1 counter on it (and no -1/-1 counters) dies. Does persist return it to the battlefield?
interactions.explanation: Persist only checks for -1/-1 counters. It returns with a -1/-1 counter.

interactions.question: I control Kudo, King Among Bears and Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite. When my opponents cast creature spells, do their creatures die as soon as they enter the battlefield?
interactions.explanation: Kudo sets every other creature's base power and toughness to 2/2 (layer 7b), and Elesh Norn gives your opponents' creatures -2/-2 (layer 7c), which always applies after the set, whatever the timestamps. So their creatures enter as 0/0 and are put into the graveyard as a state-based action. Their "enters" abilities still trigger. A creature survives only if something else boosts it, like +1/+1 counters or an anthem; and something that becomes a creature with its own set size (like a crewed Vehicle) uses that size instead of 2/2. Your own creatures are 4/4.

interactions.question: Platinum Angel is on the battlefield under my control and my life total is -3. Do I lose the game?
interactions.explanation: Platinum Angel says you can't lose the game, which overrides the state-based action. If it leaves the battlefield while you're at 0 or less life, you lose the next time state-based actions are checked.

interactions.question: Can a creature with reach block a creature with flying?
interactions.explanation: Flying only restricts what can block it: creatures with flying or reach.

interactions.question: Can a creature with flying block a creature that doesn't have flying?
interactions.explanation: Flying limits what can block the flier, not what the flier can block.

interactions.question: Can a single creature block an attacking creature with menace?
interactions.explanation: A creature with menace can't be blocked except by two or more creatures.

interactions.question: Does a creature with vigilance tap when it attacks?
interactions.explanation: Attacking doesn't cause a creature with vigilance to tap.

interactions.question: Does deathtouch work with noncombat damage, like from a fight or a pinging ability?
interactions.explanation: Any amount of damage from a source with deathtouch, combat or not, is enough to destroy a creature.

interactions.question: Does lifelink work with noncombat damage, like a creature's pinging ability?
interactions.explanation: Damage of any kind dealt by a source with lifelink makes its controller gain that much life.

interactions.question: If a creature has two instances of lifelink, do I gain double the life?
interactions.explanation: Multiple instances of lifelink on the same object are redundant.

interactions.question: My creature has double strike and lifelink. Do I gain life in both combat damage steps?
interactions.explanation: It deals combat damage twice, and each time lifelink makes you gain that much life.

interactions.question: Does indestructible stop a creature from being exiled?
interactions.explanation: Indestructible only stops a permanent from being destroyed. Exile, sacrifice, 0 toughness and bounce all still work.

interactions.question: Can I sacrifice an indestructible creature?
interactions.explanation: Sacrificing isn't destroying, so indestructible doesn't stop it.

interactions.question: Does indestructible save a creature from deathtouch damage?
interactions.explanation: Deathtouch destroys the creature, and indestructible stops it from being destroyed.

interactions.question: Can I target my own creature with hexproof with my own spells?
interactions.explanation: Hexproof only stops spells and abilities your opponents control.

interactions.question: If an opponent targets my creature with ward and doesn't pay the ward cost, is their spell countered?
interactions.explanation: Ward triggers when it becomes the target and counters the spell or ability unless its controller pays.

interactions.question: Does ward do anything against a board wipe that doesn't target, like Wrath of God?
interactions.explanation: Ward only triggers when the permanent becomes the target of an opponent's spell or ability.

interactions.question: Can I cast a creature with flash during my opponent's turn?
interactions.explanation: Flash lets you cast it any time you could cast an instant.

interactions.question: Does haste let a creature use {T} abilities the turn it comes under my control?
interactions.explanation: Haste removes summoning sickness for both attacking and {T}/{Q} abilities.

interactions.question: Can a creature with defender attack?
interactions.explanation: Defender means it can't attack.

interactions.question: Can a creature with defender block?
interactions.explanation: Defender only stops attacking; it can still block.

interactions.question: Does protection from white save a creature from Wrath of God?
interactions.explanation: Wrath of God doesn't target, deal damage, enchant or block, so protection doesn't stop it. The creature is destroyed.

interactions.question: Does protection from white prevent damage from a white creature's ability?
interactions.explanation: Protection prevents all damage from sources with that quality, combat or not.

interactions.question: My creature has an Aura of mine on it, then gains protection from the Aura's color. Does the Aura stay?
interactions.explanation: An Aura can't be attached to a permanent with protection from it, so it's put into the graveyard as a state-based action.

interactions.question: When my first-strike blocker kills the attacker in the first damage step, does the attacker deal damage back?
interactions.explanation: The attacker is gone before the regular combat damage step, so it deals no damage.

interactions.question: Does a creature with trample and lifelink gain me life for damage dealt to the player too?
interactions.explanation: Lifelink counts all damage the creature deals, to creatures and players alike.

interactions.question: Is a spell cast with flashback exiled after it resolves?
interactions.explanation: Flashback exiles the card instead of putting it anywhere else when it leaves the stack.

interactions.question: If a spell cast with flashback is countered, does it go back to my graveyard?
interactions.explanation: It's exiled, because flashback replaces any move off the stack with exile.

interactions.question: Can cascade hit a land card?
interactions.explanation: Cascade exiles until a nonland card with lower mana value.

interactions.question: Can I cast a sorcery from cascade during my opponent's turn?
interactions.explanation: You cast it while cascade resolves, which ignores the usual timing restrictions.

interactions.question: Can I tap a creature that just came in this turn to help pay a convoke cost?
interactions.explanation: Tapping for convoke isn't a {T} ability of the creature, so summoning sickness doesn't matter.

interactions.question: Can delve pay colored mana costs?
interactions.explanation: Each card exiled with delve pays for {1} of the generic cost only.

interactions.question: Does paying kicker raise a spell's mana value?
interactions.explanation: Mana value only counts the mana cost printed on the card; additional costs like kicker aren't part of it.

interactions.question: Can my opponent respond to me cycling a card?
interactions.explanation: Cycling is an activated ability, so it uses the stack and can be responded to.

interactions.question: Does madness let me cast a discarded sorcery at instant speed?
interactions.explanation: When the madness trigger resolves you may cast it right then, whatever its type.

interactions.question: Can I equip a creature I don't control?
interactions.explanation: Equip targets a creature you control.

interactions.question: If the equipped creature leaves the battlefield, does the Equipment stay on the battlefield?
interactions.explanation: The Equipment just becomes unattached and stays.

interactions.question: Does prowess trigger when I cast a creature spell?
interactions.explanation: Prowess triggers on noncreature spells only.

interactions.question: Does storm count spells my opponents cast this turn too?
interactions.explanation: Storm copies the spell once for each other spell cast before it this turn, by any player.

interactions.question: Do storm copies count as cast (for 'whenever you cast' abilities)?
interactions.explanation: Storm creates copies on the stack; they aren't cast.

interactions.question: Does annihilator make the defending player sacrifice permanents when the creature attacks?
interactions.explanation: Annihilator N triggers on attack: the defending player sacrifices N permanents.

interactions.question: Does damage from a creature with infect make a player lose life?
interactions.explanation: Infect damage to a player gives them that many poison counters instead.

interactions.question: Does exalted trigger if two of my creatures attack?
interactions.explanation: Exalted only triggers when a creature attacks alone.

interactions.question: Is a face-down morph creature a 2/2 with no name, color or abilities?
interactions.explanation: Face-down permanents are 2/2 creatures with no text, name, subtypes or mana cost.

interactions.question: When the last time counter is removed from a suspended card, do I cast it without paying its mana cost?
interactions.explanation: Suspend lets you cast it without paying its mana cost at that point.

interactions.question: If I cast a creature for its evoke cost, do its 'enters' abilities still trigger?
interactions.explanation: It enters and is sacrificed by the evoke trigger, but its own enters abilities trigger too; you choose the order.

interactions.question: Does a creature cast with dash return to my hand at the end of the turn?
interactions.explanation: Dash gives it haste and returns it to its owner's hand at the beginning of the next end step.

interactions.question: Can a Commander deck have two commanders if both have partner?
interactions.explanation: Two legendary creatures with partner can both be your commander.

interactions.question: Does a companion count as one of the 100 cards of a Commander deck?
interactions.explanation: A companion starts outside the game; it isn't part of the deck.

interactions.question: Can I mutate a creature spell onto a Human?
interactions.explanation: Mutate only goes onto a non-Human creature you own.

interactions.question: Does Cyclonic Rift cast with overload get stopped by hexproof?
interactions.explanation: Overload changes "target" to "each", so the spell doesn't target anything.

interactions.question: Can I cast a sorcery during combat?
interactions.explanation: Sorceries can only be cast in your main phase while the stack is empty.

interactions.question: Do players get priority during the untap step?
interactions.explanation: No player receives priority during the untap step, so nothing can be cast then.

interactions.question: Do players normally get priority during the cleanup step?
interactions.explanation: Only if something triggers or a state-based action happens during cleanup.

interactions.question: Can my opponent respond to a mana ability?
interactions.explanation: Mana abilities don't use the stack and resolve immediately.

interactions.question: If my spell is countered, do its 'when you cast' triggers still resolve?
interactions.explanation: They triggered when you cast it and exist on the stack independently of the spell.

interactions.question: Can I target a spell that 'can't be countered' with a counterspell?
interactions.explanation: It's still a legal target; the counterspell resolves but doesn't counter it.

interactions.question: If a creature spell is countered, does it count as dying?
interactions.explanation: "Dies" means going from the battlefield to a graveyard; a spell was never on the battlefield.

interactions.question: Does returning a creature to its owner's hand count as it dying?
interactions.explanation: "Dies" only means battlefield to graveyard.

interactions.question: Does an effect that makes spells cost {1} less reduce colored mana?
interactions.explanation: Cost reductions of generic mana only reduce the generic part of the cost.

interactions.question: When I cast a spell with X 'without paying its mana cost', what is X?
interactions.explanation: If you don't pay the mana cost, X is 0.

interactions.question: Can I pay kicker when casting a spell 'without paying its mana cost'?
interactions.explanation: You can still pay optional additional costs like kicker.

interactions.question: Can I cast a card from my graveyard just because it's there?
interactions.explanation: You need an effect or ability (like flashback) that lets you cast it from the graveyard.

interactions.question: Can I attack a planeswalker directly?
interactions.explanation: When declaring attackers, each attacker can attack a player or a planeswalker (or battle) that player controls.

interactions.question: Can a tapped creature block?
interactions.explanation: Only untapped creatures can be declared as blockers.

interactions.question: Can one creature block two attackers?
interactions.explanation: Normally each creature blocks only one attacker, unless an effect says otherwise.

interactions.question: Can several of my creatures block the same attacker?
interactions.explanation: Any number of creatures can block a single attacking creature.

interactions.question: When several creatures block one attacker, who divides its combat damage?
interactions.explanation: The attacking creature's controller divides its damage among the blockers as they choose.

interactions.question: If the only creature blocking my attacker leaves the battlefield before damage, does my attacker (without trample) deal damage to the player?
interactions.explanation: It stays blocked, and a blocked creature with no blockers deals no combat damage unless it has trample.

interactions.question: If all creatures blocking my trampler are removed before damage, can it assign all its damage to the player?
interactions.explanation: A blocked trampler with no blockers left assigns all its damage to the player.

interactions.question: If an attacking creature is removed from combat, does it deal combat damage?
interactions.explanation: A creature removed from combat stops being an attacking creature and deals no combat damage.

interactions.question: If my attacking creature gets untapped during combat, is it still attacking?
interactions.explanation: Untapping doesn't remove a creature from combat.

interactions.question: Does a double striker's 'deals combat damage to a player' ability trigger twice?
interactions.explanation: It deals combat damage in both damage steps, so it triggers each time.

interactions.question: If both players reach 0 life at the same time, what happens?
interactions.explanation: Both lose at the same time, and when all players lose simultaneously the game is a draw.

interactions.question: Does a player with ten poison counters lose even with life left?
interactions.explanation: Ten or more poison counters is a loss, no matter the life total.

interactions.question: Does a player lose right away when they try to draw from an empty library?
interactions.explanation: They lose the next time state-based actions are checked, which is almost immediately.

interactions.question: If I mill my last card, do I lose?
interactions.explanation: You only lose if you'd draw from an empty library.

interactions.question: Does damage on creatures wear off at the end of the turn?
interactions.explanation: Damage is removed from permanents during the cleanup step.

interactions.question: A 3/3 has 2 damage marked on it and then gets -1/-1. Does it die?
interactions.explanation: It's now a 2/2 with 2 damage, which is lethal damage, so it's destroyed.

interactions.question: Does a planeswalker with 0 loyalty go to the graveyard?
interactions.explanation: It's put into its owner's graveyard as a state-based action.

interactions.question: Does damage dealt to a planeswalker remove loyalty counters?
interactions.explanation: Damage to a planeswalker removes that many loyalty counters from it.

interactions.question: If two players each control a legendary creature with the same name, does the legend rule apply?
interactions.explanation: The legend rule only applies to one player controlling two or more with the same name.

interactions.question: Does the legend rule apply to two legendary creatures with different names?
interactions.explanation: It only cares about legendary permanents with the same name.

interactions.question: If a creature has three +1/+1 counters and two -1/-1 counters, what's left?
interactions.explanation: Pairs of +1/+1 and -1/-1 counters are removed as a state-based action.

interactions.question: A 1/4 creature gets +2/+0, and then its power and toughness are switched. What is it?
interactions.explanation: Switching (layer 7d) always applies after modifications (7c): it's 3/4, then switched to 4/3.

interactions.question: My creature lost all abilities to Humility, then I equip it with an Equipment that grants flying. Does it have flying?
interactions.explanation: Both apply in layer 6 by timestamp. The Equipment got a new timestamp when it was attached, after Humility, so the flying it grants is added afterward.

interactions.question: Two effects give different players control of the same creature. Who controls it?
interactions.explanation: Control-changing effects apply in layer 2 in timestamp order; the latest wins.

interactions.question: A creature with two +1/+1 counters is enchanted by an Aura that makes it a base 0/1. What is it?
interactions.explanation: Setting base power and toughness (7b) applies before counters (7c): 0/1, then +2/+2.

interactions.question: My creature has a +1/+1 counter and then becomes a copy of a 2/2. What is it?
interactions.explanation: Copy effects apply in layer 1 and only change copiable values; the counter still applies in layer 7c.

interactions.question: Does a token copy of a creature have the original's mana value?
interactions.explanation: A copy copies the mana cost, so it has the same mana value.

interactions.question: Is a token copy of a legendary creature also legendary?
interactions.explanation: It copies the supertype, so the legend rule applies to it.

interactions.question: If I copy a creature that is itself copying something, what do I get?
interactions.answer: A copy of the same thing
interactions.explanation: The copiable values of a copy are what it's copying, so you get the same result.

interactions.question: Does a copy of a spell trigger 'whenever you cast' abilities?
interactions.explanation: A copied spell is put on the stack, not cast.

interactions.question: If Clone copies a creature with an 'enters' ability, does that ability trigger for Clone?
interactions.explanation: Clone enters as a copy, so it has the ability as it enters and it triggers.

interactions.question: If two of my abilities trigger at the same time, do I choose the order they go on the stack?
interactions.explanation: Each player puts their own simultaneous triggers on the stack in any order they choose.

interactions.question: If a creature with an 'enters' trigger is destroyed in response to the trigger, does the trigger still resolve?
interactions.explanation: Once triggered, the ability exists independently of its source.

interactions.question: Does an 'at the beginning of your upkeep' ability trigger if the permanent entered during that upkeep?
interactions.explanation: The upkeep had already begun, so its trigger event has passed.

interactions.question: Do 'when this dies' abilities trigger for a creature put into the graveyard for having 0 toughness?
interactions.explanation: It went from the battlefield to the graveyard, which is dying.

interactions.question: Can a token that died be returned from the graveyard?
interactions.explanation: A token that leaves the battlefield ceases to exist the next time state-based actions are checked.

interactions.question: An ability says 'At the beginning of your upkeep, if you control ten creatures, you win the game.' If I lose a creature in response, do I still win?
interactions.explanation: An intervening "if" is checked again when the ability resolves.

interactions.question: Do 'whenever a creature enters' abilities trigger for creatures entering at the same time as the permanent with the ability?
interactions.explanation: Enters abilities look at the permanents on the battlefield after the event, including ones that entered with it.

interactions.question: Does Blood Artist trigger when my opponent's creatures die?
interactions.explanation: It triggers whenever it or another creature dies, whoever controlled that creature.

interactions.question: If a creature card is discarded from my hand, did it die?
interactions.explanation: Dying only means battlefield to graveyard.

interactions.question: Can all players look at a card exiled face up?
interactions.explanation: Exile is a public zone for face-up cards.

interactions.question: Does a creature returned from my graveyard to the battlefield have summoning sickness?
interactions.explanation: It's a new object you haven't controlled since your turn began.

interactions.question: Does a permanent that phases out leave the battlefield?
interactions.explanation: Phased-out permanents are treated as though they don't exist, but they don't change zones.

interactions.question: Do 'leaves the battlefield' abilities trigger when a permanent phases out?
interactions.explanation: Phasing out doesn't make it leave the battlefield.

interactions.question: If I steal my opponent's creature and it dies, whose graveyard does it go to?
interactions.explanation: Cards always go to their owner's graveyard, hand or library.

interactions.question: If a creature would die but an effect exiles it instead, do 'dies' abilities trigger?
interactions.explanation: The replacement effect means it never goes to the graveyard.

interactions.question: Can I tap a land that enters tapped for mana the turn it enters?
interactions.explanation: It enters the battlefield already tapped.

interactions.question: I control two effects that each double tokens being created. An effect would create one token. How many do I get?
interactions.explanation: Each replacement effect applies once, one after the other: 1 becomes 2, then 4.

interactions.question: With Doubling Season out, does a planeswalker enter with twice its loyalty?
interactions.explanation: It enters with loyalty counters, and Doubling Season doubles counters put on permanents you control.

interactions.question: With Doubling Season out, does a +1 loyalty ability give my planeswalker two counters?
interactions.explanation: Those counters are put on as a cost, not by an effect, so Doubling Season doesn't double them.

interactions.question: Does a double-faced card's back face count for its color identity?
interactions.explanation: Color identity includes both faces of a double-faced card.

interactions.question: Does reminder text count toward color identity?
interactions.explanation: Only mana symbols outside reminder text count.

interactions.question: Does commander tax apply when I cast my commander from my hand?
interactions.explanation: Commander tax only applies when casting it from the command zone.

interactions.question: Does commander tax reset when my commander goes back to the command zone?
interactions.explanation: It counts every previous cast from the command zone this game.

interactions.question: Does combat damage from a double-striking commander count twice toward commander damage?
interactions.explanation: All combat damage it deals counts, in both damage steps.

interactions.question: Does noncombat damage from a commander count toward the 21 commander damage?
interactions.explanation: Only combat damage counts toward commander damage.

interactions.question: What life total do players start with in Commander?
interactions.explanation: Each player starts at 40 life.

interactions.question: How many cards is a Commander deck, including the commander?
interactions.explanation: Exactly 100 cards, counting the commander.

interactions.question: Is a player out of a Commander game after 21 combat damage from different commanders combined?
interactions.explanation: It has to be 21 combat damage from the same commander.

interactions.question: Is sacrificing a Treasure for mana a mana ability?
interactions.explanation: It's an activated ability that makes mana and doesn't target, so it's a mana ability.

interactions.question: Can I sacrifice a Food token at instant speed?
interactions.explanation: Its ability has no timing restriction, so you can activate it whenever you have priority.

interactions.question: What is the mana value of a token that isn't a copy of anything?
interactions.explanation: An object with no mana cost has mana value 0.

interactions.question: Does maximum hand size matter at the end of my opponent's turn?
interactions.explanation: You only discard down to your hand size in your own cleanup step.

interactions.question: Can I play two lands in one turn without an effect letting me?
interactions.explanation: You can normally play one land during each of your turns.

interactions.question: Can I play a land during my opponent's turn?
interactions.explanation: Lands can only be played in your own main phase with an empty stack.

interactions.question: If I go first in a two-player game, do I draw on my first turn?
interactions.explanation: The starting player skips the draw step of their first turn in two-player games.

interactions.question: In a four-player Commander game, does the first player skip their first draw?
interactions.explanation: Only two-player games skip the first draw; in other multiplayer games everyone draws.

interactions.question: Can I sacrifice a creature I don't control?
interactions.explanation: You can only sacrifice permanents you control.

interactions.question: Can I activate a planeswalker's loyalty ability during my opponent's turn?
interactions.explanation: Loyalty abilities are sorcery-speed: your main phase, empty stack.

interactions.question: Can I activate two loyalty abilities of the same planeswalker in one turn?
interactions.explanation: Only one loyalty ability of each planeswalker per turn.

interactions.question: If my library is empty when Thassa's Oracle's enters ability resolves, do I win the game?
interactions.explanation: X (your devotion to blue) is at least 0, the number of cards in your library, so you win.

interactions.question: Can Swords to Plowshares target a creature with protection from white?
interactions.explanation: Protection from white means it can't be the target of white spells.

interactions.question: Does Teferi's Protection stop commander damage and all other damage to me?
interactions.explanation: You gain protection from everything, so all damage to you is prevented.

interactions.question: Does Craterhoof Behemoth count itself for its +X/+X?
interactions.explanation: X counts the creatures you control as the ability resolves, including Craterhoof.

interactions.question: I cast Demonic Consultation naming Thassa's Oracle while Thassa's Oracle is in my hand, then cast Thassa's Oracle. Do I win the game?
interactions.answer: Yes, when Thassa's Oracle's enters ability resolves
interactions.explanation: Demonic Consultation never reveals the named card (it's in your hand), so it exiles your whole library. That doesn't make you lose: you only lose when you'd draw from an empty library. When Thassa's Oracle's enters ability resolves, X (your devotion to blue) is at least 0, the number of cards in your library, so you win. It isn't instant: opponents can respond to Demonic Consultation, counter Thassa's Oracle, or counter its triggered ability (e.g. Stifle). Removing Thassa's Oracle in response doesn't stop it, because 0 cards is still enough.

interactions.question: Can I play Sol Ring in a Bracket 2 Commander deck?
interactions.explanation: Sol Ring isn't a Game Changer, so it fits every bracket. Brackets 1 and 2 only leave out Game Changers, two-card infinite combos and mass land denial (and extra-turn cards in Bracket 1).

interactions.question: Does my commander count toward the three Game Changers allowed in Bracket 3?
interactions.explanation: Every card in the deck counts, the commander included. A commander on the Game Changers list uses one of Bracket 3's three slots, and keeps the deck out of Brackets 1 and 2.

interactions.question: Are tutors limited in the lower Commander brackets?
interactions.explanation: The October 21, 2025 update removed the tutor limits from Brackets 1 to 3. The most efficient tutors (Demonic Tutor, Vampiric Tutor, Mystical Tutor, Worldly Tutor, Enlightened Tutor, Imperial Seal, Gamble) are Game Changers, and that covers them.

interactions.question: Is a deck with four Game Changers a Bracket 4 deck?
interactions.explanation: Bracket 3 allows up to three Game Changers, so a fourth puts the deck in Bracket 4 or 5. Brackets set a floor from the card list; a deck's intent and speed can put it higher.

interactions.question: Can a Bracket 3 deck win with an infinite combo?
interactions.answer: Yes, if it isn't an early-game two-card combo
interactions.explanation: Bracket 3 decks can win in one big turn, and combos that come together late are fine. Cheap two-card infinite combos that can win in the first few turns belong in Bracket 4 and up.

interactions.question: Is Armageddon allowed in Bracket 3?
interactions.explanation: Armageddon is mass land denial, which Brackets 1 to 3 leave out. It's fine in Brackets 4 and 5.

interactions.question: How many extra turn spells can I run in Bracket 2?
interactions.answer: A few, as long as they aren't chained or looped
interactions.explanation: Brackets 2 and 3 allow extra-turn cards in low quantities, but not taking extra turns back to back or looping them. Bracket 1 has none, and Brackets 4 and 5 have no limit.

interactions.question: What is the difference between Bracket 4 and Bracket 5 (cEDH)?
interactions.explanation: Both allow any number of Game Changers and have no other limits beyond the banned list. Bracket 5 decks are built to compete in the cEDH metagame; Bracket 4 decks are just as unrestricted but aren't tuned for that metagame.

interactions.question: Are Commander brackets enforced by judges at tournaments?
interactions.explanation: Brackets are optional guidelines for finding a fair game, agreed on before playing. They aren't in the Comprehensive Rules or the tournament rules, and the Commander banned list still applies in every bracket.

interactions.question: Where does the Game Changers list come from and how often does it change?
interactions.answer: The Commander Format Panel, every few months
interactions.explanation: Wizards and the Commander Format Panel keep the list and review it every few months; the latest change (February 9, 2026) added Farewell and Biorhythm. The app reads the current list from Scryfall with the card database.
